Definition: to turn away, i.e. (morally) be refractory
BiblicalUsage: The Old Testament word çârar means to turn away, to be refractory. It appears 16 times, and the passages that use it — Deuteronomy and Hosea among them — show it in its natural setting. Read them together and the meaning settles itself.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God chose çârar on purpose. To turn away, to be refractory is not an accident of language; it is the way He says what He means.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
